argument_summary: Certification is supportable only on a narrow, caveated basis. The admissible record shows aggregate launch readiness cleared by 2.4 percentage points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a reversible 3% monitored rollout. That does not justify a claim that rollout controls cure the weakness, because the health-plan benefits support segment remains below target on benefits-eligibility explanation and remains exposed in the initial cohort. The supportable position is certify with explicit model-card disclosure of that limitation at launch, while treating monitoring and rollback as secondary containment.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to support this position. The requested treatment is limited to avoiding unnecessary escalation where the existing admissible record supports certification with a launch disclosure caveat and deployment monitoring.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy does not permit rollout controls alone to eliminate disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed. Because the initial cohort still includes the weak health-plan benefits support segment and the available risk acceptance is unsigned and does not cover that exposure, the compliant path is disclosure-backed certification rather than a clean claim that controls resolve the issue.
concessions: The exposed health-plan benefits support segment is below target on benefits-eligibility explanation.
The initial 3% rollout does not exclude that affected segment.
The draft risk acceptance cannot be relied on because it is unsigned and does not address the exposed segment.
This is not clean compliance on the theory that rollout controls alone are sufficient; it is supportable only with explicit launch disclosure.
